study: Arthi, Beach & Hanlon (2022), Recessions, Mortality, and Migration Bias: Evidence from the Lancashire Cotton Famine
human_benchmark: Dupraz (2023), I4R DP No. 25 / AEJ:Applied public comment (2025); flora=computationally reproducible (reproduced Figures 1-4 and Tables 1-5 from authors' code+data)
key_findings: The authors' OA replication package (OpenICPSR project 128521, ABH_Rep, CC BY 4.0) and the I4R repliers' package (OpenICPSR 192272, Dupraz_I4R_ABH_Rep) both exist and are publicly listed, but ALL file content routes (folder/file view, download/terms, /api/... filetree) return HTTP 403 behind a Cloudflare 'managed challenge' that requires JS proof-of-work, so no .do/.dta file could be retrieved.
No OSF/GitHub mirror exists: the OSF node (osf.io/fxta6) is a metadata hub with zero files, pointing back to the same gated OpenICPSR packages and to the EconStor-gated I4R report.

The I4R DP25 / published AEA comment full text is reachable only via EconStor, which is protected by Anubis (JS proof-of-work); webfetch could not pass it. The AEA 'Public (Legacy) Comment' materials item is only a 1-page pointer to the OSF entry.
The original AEJ:Applied paper is paywalled with no OA copy (OpenAlex best_oa_location null); no NBER/working-paper OA version located.

Consequently headline numerical claims (Tables 1-5 point estimates, Figures 1-4) could not be independently re-computed. Specific figures from the original paper were NOT obtained and are NOT asserted in this audit.

Via open metadata (RWI/I4R/IDEAS/OSF abstracts) the human benchmark reports: ABH results fully reproducible from data+code; robust to narrower age window, modified specification, and different SEs; the only discrepancy is stronger famine effects under a narrower linking-age window (attributed to reduced measurement error). Authors signed off on the I4R report.
notes: Data_access_wall: OpenICPSR (authors 128521 and I4R repliers 192272) is Cloudflare-challenged to automated/non-browser clients; EconStor (report) is Anubis-challenged; Wayback Machine offline during audit. Data is public-for-humans (CC BY 4.0), so this is an accessibility/technical wall, NOT missing data and NOT a reproducibility defect. AI verdict on reproduciBILITY could not be independently reached; matches the human 'computationally reproducible' classification only in the sense of no counter-evidence, not via my own re-run. No Paywalled PDFs retained in audit folder.
